title: Pecan Snowball Cookies
subtitle: buttery, nutty little balls that melt in your mouth, rolled twice in icing sugar
imageAlt: Round cookies thickly coated in white icing sugar heaped on a white plate on a navy napkin
servingsNote: about 30 cookies: 3 each, and a tin to give away

beforeYouStart.text: Soft butter: it should dent easily but not look greasy. Leave it out about an hour.
Chop the pecans fine, about the size of rice, so the balls hold together.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line 2 baking sheets with parchment. Beat the butter, icing sugar, vanilla and salt about 2 minutes, until light.

steps.title: Add flour and pecans
steps.text: Mix in the flour on low until crumbly, then the pecans, until the dough holds together when squeezed.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll into 2.5 cm balls (about 20 g) and set them 3 cm apart on the sheets.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake both sheets 13–15 minutes, swapping racks halfway, until the bottoms are light golden and the tops still pale.

steps.title: First roll
steps.text: Cool 5 minutes, then roll the warm cookies in the icing sugar and set on a rack to cool completely.

steps.title: Second roll
steps.text: Roll the cooled cookies in the rest of the icing sugar for a thick white coat.

fixIt.fix: Squeeze and knead it a few times with your hands; the warmth brings it together.
The butter was too soft. Chill the shaped balls 15 minutes before baking.

fixIt.problem: Icing sugar melted into a glaze
fixIt.fix: They were too hot for the first roll. Wait the full 5 minutes; the second roll covers any patches.
Use a light-coloured sheet, or bake on the middle rack only, one sheet at a time.

saleTip: Pecans are the pricey part. Watch for the 200 g bags on sale in December, or use walnuts, which are often cheaper.
swap: Walnuts or almonds: same amount, finely chopped.
leftovers: Crush over ice cream or fold into whipped cream for a quick dessert.
doneness: Bottoms light golden, tops still pale. They're tender out of the oven and firm up as they cool.
source: Based on tested snowball / Russian tea cake methods (Canadian Living, Betty Crocker): a nutty butter dough with no eggs, baked at 180°C (350°F) and rolled twice in icing sugar.
prepAhead: Make the dough up to 2 days ahead and keep it wrapped in the fridge; let it soften 20 minutes before shaping.
Freeze baked, once-rolled cookies; give them the second roll after thawing.
reheat: Not needed. Serve at room temperature.

stepNotes.1: Basic: no pecans; mix just until the dough holds together.

fancy.note: Toasted pecans and a cinnamon-spiced coat.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: first toast the chopped pecans in a dry skillet over medium 3–4 minutes until fragrant, and cool them.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: stir the cinnamon into the rolling sugar first.

plating: Pile them in a pyramid on a dark plate.
Mini paper cups make them easy to give away.

why.0-1: Icing sugar in the dough (not granulated) is what makes them melt in your mouth.
why.1-0: The first roll sticks to the warm cookie; the second gives the thick snowy coat.

funFact: The same cookie goes by Russian tea cakes, Mexican wedding cookies and Italian butter balls; nobody agrees where it started.

keeps.thaw: On the counter about 1 hour, then the second roll
